memoryText: If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Luke 9:23 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Jesus says this just after Peter’s confession and his first prediction of his death. He says it to everyone: “If anyone would come after me.” It is an open invitation and a hard one.

“Deny himself.” This does not mean to hate yourself or to lose your identity. It means to say no to the self that sits on the throne. To follow Jesus is to stop being the center of your own life.

“Take up his cross.” The cross was not a symbol of jewelry in the first century. It was an instrument of public execution, and a person who carried one was walking to his death. Jesus calls his followers to a life of surrender, willing to lose reputation, comfort, and control for his sake.

“Daily.” Luke alone adds this word. The cross is not a single dramatic moment but a daily rhythm. Every morning we choose again.

“And follow me.” The road is not an empty road. We follow someone who went before us, and he did not ask us to carry anything he did not carry first. The next verse gives the promise: whoever loses his life for Jesus’ sake will save it.

When you are tempted to protect your comfort, say this verse. The way of the cross is the way of life.
weekInReview: This week you sang Psalm 116, the thanks of someone saved from death, and Psalm 117, the shortest call to the nations. In Luke 7 and 8 you saw Jesus honor a centurion’s faith, raise a widow’s son, forgive a woman who loved much, and teach about the soils of the heart. You watched him still a storm, free a demoniac, and raise Jairus’s daughter. You heard Peter confess him as the Christ of God and the Father say, “Listen to him.” On the road to Jerusalem you met the Good Samaritan, sat with Mary at Jesus’ feet, and learned to pray. You heard warnings against greed and hypocrisy and the promise to the little flock that the Father is pleased to give the kingdom.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said Mary chose the good portion by sitting at his feet. What would it look like for you to make listening to him the first thing in your day?
In Luke 9:20, Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ of God, and then Jesus spoke of the cross. How does Jesus’ own suffering shape what it means to follow him?
The rich fool stored up treasure for himself and was not rich toward God. What is one way you can be rich toward God this week?
prayerPrompts: Tell Jesus you want to follow him and say what that costs you.
Ask him to teach you to take up your cross daily.
